projects.name: Microsoft GraphRAG

paper.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

projects.what: Reference GraphRAG: LLM entity/relation extraction, Leiden communities, community reports; global and local (and DRIFT) search.
projects.graph_build: LLM extracts entities + relations + claims per chunk; Leiden hierarchical communities; LLM summary per community.
projects.requirements: Python 3.10-3.12, OpenAI-compatible LLM + embeddings; parquet/LanceDB storage
projects.strengths: The canonical baseline every paper compares against; prompt tuning; well documented.
projects.limits: Indexing is expensive (many LLM calls); untyped free-text relations; global search weak on fact lookups.
projects.evidence: abstract read; README read earlier (Toolbox note)

projects.name: LightRAG

paper.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
paper.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

projects.what: Graph + vector RAG with dual-level (low/high keyword) retrieval and incremental index updates; many storage backends and a web UI.
projects.graph_build: LLM extracts entities and relations with keyword profiles per chunk; merges duplicates by name; no communities.
projects.requirements: Python, any OpenAI-compatible / Ollama LLM; Neo4j, PostgreSQL(AGE+pgvector), Qdrant, Milvus etc. optional
projects.strengths: Cheap incremental indexing; easy to point at Alibaba/AvalAI; strong community; server + UI.
projects.limits: Relation types are free text; reported wins come from LLM-judge win-rates, later benchmarks are mixed.

projects.name: HippoRAG 1/2

paper.title: From RAG to Memory: Non-Parametric Continual Learning for Large Language Models

extra_papers.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

projects.what: Memory-inspired RAG: OpenIE triples form a KG; Personalized PageRank from query entities ranks passages. v2 adds passage nodes and recognition memory.
projects.graph_build: OpenIE (LLM) triples + synonym edges by embedding similarity; passages linked to their phrases (v2).
retrieval: PPR over KG seeded by query triples/entities
projects.requirements: Python, vLLM or OpenAI LLM, embedding model (NV-Embed-v2 default, GPU helpful)
projects.strengths: Strong multi-hop QA with cheap indexing; clean reproducible eval scripts; continual-learning framing.
projects.limits: Factoid multi-hop focus; no community summaries; default embedder needs a GPU.

projects.name: GraphRAG-Bench (When to use graphs)

paper.title: When to use Graphs in RAG: A Comprehensive Analysis for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

projects.what: Benchmark + harness: when do graphs help RAG? Tasks from fact retrieval to creative generation; evaluates graph construction and retrieval.
projects.graph_build: Runs the systems under test (LightRAG, HippoRAG, MS GraphRAG, ...).
projects.strengths: Ready harness to compare RAG vs GraphRAG fairly.

projects.name: Graphusion / TutorQA

paper.title: Graphusion: A RAG Framework for Knowledge Graph Construction with a Global Perspective

projects.what: Zero-shot KG construction for NLP-course concepts with global fusion; TutorQA expert-verified benchmark of course QA tasks.
projects.graph_build: Seed concepts (topic modelling) -> LLM triple extraction (prerequisite etc.) -> global fusion and conflict resolution.
projects.strengths: Course concept KG + education QA benchmark: directly our domain.
projects.limits: Small repo (about 30 stars); NLP-course only; no licence file; needs OpenAI/Google keys + Neo4j.

projects.name: GraphRAG-Bench (domain-specific, textbooks)

paper.title: GraphRAG-Bench: Challenging Domain-Specific Reasoning for Evaluating Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

projects.what: Domain-specific GraphRAG benchmark: college-level questions (5 types: fill-in-blank, multiple-choice, multi-select, true/false, open-ended) over a 7M-word corpus from 20 computer-science textbooks; scores answers and rationales.
projects.graph_build: Runs systems under test on textbook corpora.
projects.strengths: CS textbook questions = closest public analogue to our course question bank.

projects.name: DeepTutor
projects.what: Open personalised tutor from the LightRAG team: KB over course PDFs, problem solving, question generation, guided learning.
projects.graph_build: LightRAG / RAG-Anything knowledge base.
projects.strengths: Closest open reference architecture for a course tutor.

projects.name: neo4j-graphrag-python
projects.what: Official Neo4j GraphRAG package: SimpleKGPipeline (schema-guided extraction), vector, hybrid, VectorCypher and Text2Cypher retrievers.
projects.graph_build: Schema-guided LLM extraction (node types, relationship types, patterns) into Neo4j, with lexical graph of chunks.
projects.requirements: Neo4j 5.x, Python; any LLM via adapters
projects.strengths: Typed schema in Neo4j, close to the thesis stack; maintained by Neo4j. We did not use it to build the graph (our own extraction code with Opus 5.5).

projects.name: DIGIMON (unified GraphRAG framework)

paper.title: In-depth Analysis of Graph-based RAG in a Unified Framework

projects.what: One codebase that re-implements ~10 graph-based RAG methods (RAPTOR, LightRAG, HippoRAG, GraphRAG, ToG, G-Retriever, ...) with shared operators.
projects.graph_build: Configurable: passage graph, tree, KG, rich KG, etc.
retrieval: operator library: entity, relation, chunk, subgraph, community
projects.strengths: Fair side-by-side comparison of GraphRAG variants: exactly our evaluation need.
projects.limits: No licence file (reuse needs permission); last push 2025-07.

projects.name: nano-graphrag
projects.what: ~1k-line hackable re-implementation of Microsoft GraphRAG (local, global, naive modes).
projects.graph_build: Same pipeline as MS GraphRAG (LLM extraction, Leiden communities, reports) in compact code.
projects.requirements: Python; pluggable LLM, vector DB and graph storage (networkx, Neo4j)
projects.strengths: Easiest code to read and modify for typed-relation ablations.
projects.limits: No paper; less maintained than upstream.

projects.name: RAPTOR

paper.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval

projects.what: Recursive clustering and summarising of chunks into a tree; retrieval over all tree levels.
projects.graph_build: Tree, not KG: GMM/UMAP clusters of chunk embeddings, LLM summary per cluster, recursively.
projects.strengths: Simple hierarchical baseline that fits lecture->section->concept structure.

projects.name: SubgraphRAG

paper.title: Simple Is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation

projects.what: Lightweight MLP + directional distance encoding scores triples; retrieves a size-tunable subgraph for any LLM.
projects.graph_build: Existing KG (WebQSP, CWQ).
projects.strengths: Shows simple retrieval + strong LLM is enough; triple-level evidence.

projects.name: FlashRAG

paper.title: FlashRAG: A Modular Toolkit for Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation Research

projects.what: Research toolkit: 20+ RAG methods, 36 benchmark datasets, unified pipelines and metrics.
projects.graph_build: Mostly none (some methods add structure).
projects.strengths: Reproducible plain-RAG baselines and metrics.

projects.name: RAGAS

paper.title: Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
paper.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

projects.what: Reference-free RAG metrics: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall; test-set generation.
projects.graph_build: Knowledge graph used internally for synthetic test-set generation.
projects.strengths: Standard metric names reviewers expect.
projects.limits: LLM-judge metrics need validation against humans.

projects.name: fast-graphrag
projects.what: Cheaper GraphRAG with a domain + entity-type schema and PageRank-based exploration.
projects.graph_build: LLM extraction constrained by user-given entity types and domain prompt; incremental.
projects.strengths: Typed schema close to our typed-relations idea; low cost.

projects.name: KAG (OpenSPG)

paper.title: KAG: Boosting LLMs in Professional Domains via Knowledge Augmented Generation

projects.what: Knowledge-augmented generation: schema-constrained KG (OpenSPG) + logical-form solver mixing graph reasoning and text retrieval.
projects.graph_build: Schema-guided extraction with mutual indexing between chunks and graph nodes; knowledge alignment.
projects.strengths: Typed schema and reasoning for professional domains.

projects.name: PathRAG

paper.title: PathRAG: Pruning Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation with Relational Paths

projects.what: Prunes graph retrieval to key relational paths (flow-based pruning) and prompts with paths, built on LightRAG.
projects.graph_build: LightRAG-style LLM extraction.
projects.strengths: Path-level evidence suits prerequisite chains in courses.

projects.name: GNN-RAG

paper.title: GNN-RAG: Graph Neural Retrieval for Large Language Model Reasoning

projects.what: GNN reasons over a KG subgraph to pick answer candidates; shortest paths to them are verbalised for the LLM.
projects.graph_build: Existing KG (Freebase: WebQSP, CWQ).
projects.strengths: Strong KGQA; path verbalisation is reusable.

projects.name: RAGChecker

paper.title: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation

projects.what: Claim-level diagnosis of retriever and generator (claim recall, context utilisation, noise sensitivity, hallucination).
projects.graph_build: n/a
projects.strengths: Diagnoses which stage fails: fits the ablation story.

projects.name: InstructKG
projects.what: Builds concept-dependency KGs from lecture slides and textbooks with multi-LLM roles.
projects.graph_build: 5 stages: PDF chunking, LLM concept extraction with roles (definition, application, prerequisite), context clustering, concept-pair generation, LLM relation judging.
projects.strengths: Same input as ours (lecture material).
projects.limits: Tiny repo (2 stars), no paper link found.

projects.name: Graphiti (Zep)

paper.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory

projects.what: Temporal (bi-temporal) KG memory for agents; incremental episodes; hybrid search.
projects.graph_build: LLM extraction of entities/edges per episode with custom typed entities (Pydantic), temporal edge invalidation.
projects.strengths: Per-learner memory with typed entities; very active.

projects.name: Neo4j LLM Graph Builder
projects.what: App that turns PDFs, web pages and YouTube into a Neo4j KG (chunks + entities) and offers several chat modes.
projects.graph_build: LangChain LLMGraphTransformer with optional schema; chunk lexical graph; community summaries.
projects.strengths: Fastest way to see a typed course KG in Neo4j and compare chat modes.

projects.name: LlamaIndex (PropertyGraphIndex)
projects.what: RAG framework; PropertyGraphIndex builds labelled property graphs with schema-guided or free extractors and mixes graph + vector retrieval.
projects.graph_build: SchemaLLMPathExtractor (typed), SimpleLLMPathExtractor, ImplicitPathExtractor.
projects.strengths: Fast prototyping of typed vs untyped extraction.

projects.name: iText2KG

paper.title: iText2KG: Incremental Knowledge Graphs Construction Using Large Language Models

projects.what: Incremental, schema-light KG construction with entity and relation resolution; Neo4j export.
projects.graph_build: LLM extraction per document, embedding-based entity/relation merging, incremental.
projects.strengths: Entity resolution step we need for course KGs.

projects.name: KGGen

paper.title: KGGen: Extracting Knowledge Graphs from Plain Text with Language Models

projects.what: Text-to-KG with LLM extraction plus iterative clustering of equivalent entities and relations; MINE benchmark.
projects.graph_build: LLM triples, then clustering to merge synonyms (entities and relation labels).
projects.strengths: Relation-label normalisation: useful for typed relations.

projects.name: Youtu-GraphRAG

paper.title: Youtu-GraphRAG: Vertically Unified Agents for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Complex Reasoning

projects.what: Agentic GraphRAG with a schema-bounded extraction agent, community tree and agentic retriever.
projects.graph_build: Seed schema (entity/relation/attribute types) that the agent expands; dually-perceived community detection.
projects.strengths: Schema-bounded typed relations, close to the thesis design.

projects.name: G-Retriever

paper.title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering

projects.what: Textual-graph QA: Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree subgraph retrieval + GNN soft prompt for an LLM.
projects.graph_build: Uses existing textual graphs (ExplaGraphs, SceneGraphs, WebQSP).
projects.strengths: Subgraph retrieval idea.

projects.name: GFM-RAG

paper.title: GFM-RAG: Graph Foundation Model for Retrieval Augmented Generation

projects.what: Graph foundation model (query-dependent GNN) as a retriever over a KG index built from documents.
projects.graph_build: OpenIE KG index from documents (HippoRAG-style).
projects.strengths: Pretrained checkpoint usable zero-shot.

projects.name: MiniRAG

paper.title: MiniRAG: Towards Extremely Simple Retrieval-Augmented Generation

projects.what: Graph RAG tuned for small language models via a heterogeneous chunk-entity graph and topology-driven retrieval.
projects.graph_build: Heterogeneous graph of text chunks and named entities (light extraction).
projects.strengths: Relevant if we test small local models.

projects.name: KET-RAG

paper.title: KET-RAG: A Cost-Efficient Multi-Granular Indexing Framework for Graph-RAG

projects.what: Cost-efficient multi-granular index: KG skeleton on key chunks + text-keyword bipartite graph.
projects.graph_build: LLM KG only for selected core chunks; keyword-chunk bipartite graph for the rest.
projects.strengths: Cost per correct answer focus: matches our metric.

projects.name: Reasoning on Graphs (RoG)

paper.title: Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning

projects.what: Planning-retrieval-reasoning: LLM generates relation paths as plans, retrieves matching KG paths, reasons over them.
projects.graph_build: Existing KG (Freebase).
projects.strengths: Typed relation paths as plans: very close to typed-relations retrieval.

projects.name: LinearRAG

paper.title: LinearRAG: Linear Graph Retrieval Augmented Generation on Large-scale Corpora

projects.what: Relation-free 'Tri-Graph' (entities, sentences, passages) built without LLM relation extraction; two-stage retrieval.
projects.graph_build: Lightweight entity extraction + semantic linking; no relation extraction.
projects.strengths: Argues relation extraction is noisy: a useful counterpoint for the typed-relations ablation.

projects.name: Think-on-Graph (ToG)

paper.title: Think-on-Graph: Deep and Responsible Reasoning of Large Language Model on Knowledge Graph

projects.graph_build: Existing KG (Freebase, Wikidata).
retrieval: iterative LLM beam search on KG
projects.requirements: Python, LLM API, KG SPARQL endpoint
projects.strengths: Training-free agentic KG exploration.

projects.strengths: Lecture slides and PDFs with formulas.

radar.note: Where we look for new RAG and GraphRAG papers with code. 'Measured' = an HTTP or API call on the date; 'read' = the page was opened and its text read; 'not read' = we could not see it.

sources.name: Papers with Code (paperswithcode.co)
sources.offers: Trending and recent ML papers, a paper archive, research tasks, methods, datasets and evaluation results. A paper page shows the TL;DR, abstract, arXiv and PDF links, several code repositories (official or not, with stars), tasks and methods. Example: the GraphRAG paper (2404.16130) lists microsoft/graphrag, nano-graphrag and graphrag-local-ollama.
sources.api: Yes: an anonymous, read-only public API, 'experimental beta' (OpenAPI 1.0.0-beta at /api/v1/openapi.json). Endpoints for papers (search, recent, trending, by arXiv id with repositories), tasks, datasets, evaluations. Its own description: 'Keyword search and bounded lookups; not a bulk export service.' No bulk data export was found.
sources.vs_old: The old paperswithcode.com (Meta) now redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers (HTTP 302, measured) and its data lives on only as the frozen pwc-archive datasets on Hugging Face (2025-09). paperswithcode.co is a separate live service with its own API and fresh data (papers dated 2026-10, citation counts refreshed). It marks one repository as official: for HippoRAG 1 it lists osu-nlp-group/hipporag as official, where the HF Papers link points to the wrong repo.
sources.use: Paper to code lookup with official flag; trending list as a radar. Cross-check repositories against the paper's abstract or README.
sources.evidence: read: home page and the GraphRAG paper page (headless browser); measured: /api/v1/papers/arxiv/2404.16130 and 2405.14831, /api/v1/openapi.json, /health
sources.not_read: Who runs the service, its terms of use and rate limits: the API documentation page (/docs/api) and the privacy page did not render in the headless browser. The relation to the original Papers with Code team is unverified.

sources.name: Hugging Face Papers
sources.offers: Daily and trending papers; the API (huggingface.co/api/papers/<arXiv id>) returns a githubRepo field when the authors or users linked one.
sources.api: Yes: public JSON API per paper, no key.
sources.vs_old: The official successor that paperswithcode.com redirects to.
sources.use: Live paper to code links and what is popular.
sources.evidence: measured: 39 papers via the API; the code link is missing for 18 of 39 and wrong for HippoRAG 1 (it points to circlemind-ai/fast-graphrag)

sources.name: GitHub
sources.offers: Stars, last push, licence, archived flag, the README and the code itself.
sources.api: Yes: REST and gh CLI (gh api repos/OWNER/NAME, gh search repos).
sources.use: The numbers that decide reuse: is it maintained, what licence, how big.
sources.evidence: measured for every project and tool on these pages

sources.name: Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex
sources.offers: Citation counts, influential citations, citation graph and related papers (Semantic Scholar); bulk counts and lists (OpenAlex).
sources.api: Yes: Semantic Scholar Graph API (no key here, rate limited) and the OpenAlex API.
sources.use: Dated citation counts on every paper link; OpenAlex as a cross-check.
sources.evidence: measured: Semantic Scholar batch API for 38 papers, OpenAlex for one

trademark: Logos are shown only to identify each project; trademarks belong to their owners.
